note: A single pull-in gravel site in partial shade for up to six people at the start of the Gobbler's Roost Trail on Eagleton Road, about 5.5 miles from PA 120, with access to the Eagleton Mine Camp Trail System (mountain biking, horseback riding and hiking). The booking page sells it for RVs and trailers, while the DCNR campsite map layer marks it as having no trailer access. The agency cautions that it is reached by remote dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. No table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: SS025 still listed, Drive-In, Horse/RV/Tent/Trailer categories, max vehicle 30 ft (equipment length 25), pull-in gravel driveway 25 ft; count 1 and 30 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; sells in all five windows. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri and PASDA): pin under conifer canopy about 60 m north of a gravel road with a gravel spur or lot to the south-east; pad not visible, pin not moved. NHD: nothing within 200 m; not waterfront.
flags: Ruling 5 applied: the booking page lists 'RV Site ... Trailer Site' with Max Vehicle Length 30, while the DCNR GIS record for SS025 says 'TrailerAccess: No' (record notes 'Added December 2024'). Kept, both statements in the note.

Figures: 'Max Vehicle Length: 30', 'Equipment Length: 25', 'Driveway Length: 25', 'Length of shortest side of spur to the wheelstop: 6', site 62 x 33 ft. Max Vehicle and Equipment Length are 23 ft or more but the spur figure is 6 ft: kept at 30 ft with all figures in the sites note.

Horse category: the page lists 'Horse Site' among four categories and describes access to a trail system open to horseback riding. It is not a horse camp (not one of the agency's named equestrian areas) and RV and trailer categories are sold; kept.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by remote state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' No grade lines, no Severe grade, no 4WD, wet-weather or low-clearance statement (clearance 40 ft). Kept. Boilerplate on every page of the district, not site-specific: 'State forest roads are not maintained in the winter and often become snow covered, icy and potentially impassable' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).

ATV check (ruling 1): nothing on the site page, GIS record or district map places this site in an ATV parking lot. Kept. The Eagleton Mine Camp trails the page names are for mountain biking, horseback riding and hiking.

Sproul advisories page (read 2026-11-10): nothing on this site's road. It carries a Bloody Skillet ATV section closure (April 20, 2026), the indefinite Left Branch Young Womans Creek Road closure, 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads' and a dust advisory.
